name: Tessier Number 5 Facial Cleft

criteria.description: Presence of a cleft extending from the oral commissure obliquely towards the infraorbital region
Soft tissue deficiency along the cleft line including skin and muscle involvement
Bony defects involving the maxilla and/or zygomatic bone corresponding to the cleft path
Possible involvement of the lower eyelid or infraorbital rim abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of the characteristic oblique facial cleft extending from the oral commissure to the infraorbital region with associated soft tissue and bony defects
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging studies to assess bony involvement.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Oblique facial cleft extending from oral commissure to infraorbital region

imaging: CT scan showing maxillary and zygomatic bone defects along cleft path
MRI to evaluate soft tissue and possible intracranial involvement
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence common
Possible association with craniofacial developmental gene disruptions
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic oblique facial cleft

distinguishingFeatures: Cleft extends from philtrum to medial canthus rather than oral commissure to infraorbital region
Lateral facial cleft extending from oral commissure towards ear
Involves macrostomia and facial musculature differently

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
Respiratory distress due to airway obstruction
Signs of intracranial anomalies or neurological deficits
